authority: Operator decision returned in plans/fieldwise_operator_input_pack.md item 4, folded into Tier 3 by plans/fieldwise_tickets.md ticket 6. Recorded per CLAUDE.md §9.4; status per §12.2.
decision: Supervision cadence, a Project Steering Group, a decision-rights table, a conflict-resolution route and one named contact per partner organisation are adopted as drafted, with three amendments the co-supervisor's appointment forced and one correction to the escalation route.
why: The draft names four corrective decision points at M6, M12, M16 and M20 and describes the two-way transfer, but defines no bodies, no cadence and no decision rights. phase_06_gate predicate g07_p07 requires at least one governance body with composition and decision scope, and g07_p08 requires every management role to name a partner that exists in partners.json.
amendments_for_the_co_supervisor: Supervision cadence gains a weekly technical session with the CO_SUPERVISOR through WP3 and WP4 (M6-M21), tapering to monthly outside that window. It was raised from fortnightly once the operator confirmed he is responsible for model development and testing.

The decision-rights table gains one row: model development and testing, methodological lead and quality assurance, owned by CO_SUPERVISOR and escalating to SUPERVISOR. The wording is deliberate — it matches authority to responsibility while keeping the fellow as the person who designs, builds and runs the models.
The CO_SUPERVISOR attends the Steering Group as a member. He does not chair and adds no partner seat: he is ELTE staff, and ELTE is already represented by the chair.

contradictions_resolved.what: The fellow held the MVCRI contact seat and the TRANSFER_PARTNER seat on a body that issues go/no-go verdicts on the milestones her own model is tested against, and the decision-rights table routed data-access disputes to the owning partner, escalating to that same body.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Prof. Vinelina Yankova, Head of the Department of Technologies in Vegetable Crops Production, takes both seats. The fellow sits once, as FELLOW, and the escalation is genuine.

contradictions_resolved.what: The accepted conflict-resolution route escalated past the SUPERVISOR to the head of the ELTE Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics, of which the supervisor is himself deputy — so the route partly looped back on the person being escalated past.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: The route names the Director of the Institute as an OFFICE, not a person. The Director and the Deputy Director are different posts, so the loop is broken, and an office-based route survives a change of incumbent across a 30-month action. The incumbent Director is not associated with the call and is named nowhere in Tier 3. The alternative the operator left open — escalating straight to the ELTE research integrity route — removes the local step that usually resolves things fastest and was not taken.

gate_effect: phase_06_gate g07_p07 passes on the Steering Group. g07_p08 resolves: MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR all exist in consortium/partners.json, and the CO_SUPERVISOR resolves to ELTE, present as HOST.
open: Only one of the three partner contacts carries a verified title (Yankova). Takács at MATE and Balázs at AgroVIR are names without roles, and both are Assumed with declarations in working_assumptions.json. Item 6's Career Development Plan should be signed by both supervisors and the fellow, which CC-13's 'established jointly' requires and item 6's accepted answer does not say.
